newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds end little changed, underperform.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds end little changed, underperform.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in very quiet trade on Friday on a lack of economic data, with Canada slightly underperforming U.S. bonds amid recent weakness in the currency, analysts said.

"We really didn't have any economic numbers to move the market," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc. "In Canada, the only story was the dollar when we first came in."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.05 to C$108.60 to yield 7.260 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 4/32 to yield 7.06 percent.
The spread between the two bonds widened to 20 basis points from 19 basis points on Thursday.

Canada's dollar opened weaker on Friday at C$1.4009 (US$0.7138), after trading as low as C$1.4024 (US$0.7131) in overnight markets. The currency weakened to two-year lows in recent weeks amid concern that a near-term rise in U.S. interest rates would not be matched by the Bank of Canada.

"Speculation over a possible Canadian rate hike heightened once again as the Canadian dollar dropped to another low in early morning activity," David Ebata, a Canadian market analysts with Technical Data, said in a commentary.
The Canadian dollar recovered slightly later in the session, ending little changed for the week.

Activity in Canadian and U.S. bond markets was light, with the release of the Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index being the only major data out in either country. The report had little impact on the market.
In other prices, the Canadian 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.04 to C$102.06 to yield 6.704 percent.
The U.S. bond rose 4/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 13 basis points, unchanged from Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.22 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.29 percent.
